discovery: Prediction and experimental discovery of the quantum anomalous Hall effect

motivation: The quantum Hall effect was thought to require strong magnetic fields and Landau levels. Haldane's 1988 model showed that quantized Hall conductance could in principle occur without them, but for 25 years nobody knew how to realize it. In 2010 Zhong Fang and Xi Dai, with collaborators, predicted that magnetically doped Bi2Se3-family topological insulator thin films would host a quantized anomalous Hall state driven by intrinsic magnetization. In 2013 Qi-Kun Xue's team spent years perfecting molecular-beam epitaxy of Cr-doped (Bi,Sb)2Te3 films and observed the quantized Hall resistance h/e² at zero field, with vanishing longitudinal resistance. This was a true '0 to 1' discovery: a new quantum state of matter, independently reproduced worldwide. It established dissipationless chiral edge transport and opened the field of magnetic topological materials, including MnBi2Te4 and moiré Chern insulators. Theory, materials control and precision measurement came together to make it possible.
